subject: muzzleflash1
label: sprites/muzzleflash1.spr, in the place of the game's own

R1.reason: The brief asks for a short bright burst of fire in a star shape. Frames 0 to 2 show a star-shaped glint: a white core with six to eight thin pale spikes and no flame or tongues of fire. It reads as a lens-style flare more than a muzzle blast.

R2.reason: Measured at 64 x 64 with border max 0, so nothing touches the frame edge. The star fills roughly the middle 70% of each cell, which suits a burst. Each frame is the same size and centred.

R3.reason: Judged by eye, not measured. The core is near-white and the spikes are warm amber-yellow on the dark background, which reads as bright, hot light. The brief sets no colour, and this fits its 'bright burst of fire'.

R4.reason: The brief asks for two frames. The sprite has four: frames 0, 1 and 2 are lit and frame 3 (the last) is fully dark. The envelope (first 0.84, peak at 0.33, last 0) is a fade that ends dark, which the one-shot needs. The class's frame count is not among the given againstClass measures, so the four-frame count cannot be confirmed against Half-Life's own flares. It is also not the two frames the brief asks for, and frame 3 is a wasted blank.

R5.reason: Type 'parallel' and format 'additive' match the game's own (gameType and gameFormat both parallel and additive). sameName is true and readsBack is true, so the file is read back as written.
